what: Astera Labs makes connectivity chips for AI data centres: the retimers, switches and controllers that keep high-speed signals intact between processors, accelerators and memory inside a server rack.
customers: Cloud and AI infrastructure operators, server manufacturers and chip companies building AI systems.
money: PCIe and Ethernet connectivity chips, modules and the software that manages them
moat: Designed into AI server platforms years ahead, with diagnostic software that data centre operators rely on and would have to replace alongside the chips.
risks: Revenue depends on a handful of very large cloud customers
Broadcom and Marvell can bundle connectivity with their larger chip sales
A slowdown in AI server building would hit it immediately
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 115% last year and about 120% a year over three years
Gross margin of 76% with cash of $1.4 billion and almost no debt
Each new AI rack generation needs more connectivity content than the last
watch: Quarterly revenue guidance and customer concentration.
